pages.title: What it does
text: It drives the vanilla minecraft:knockback_resistance attribute, ranging from 0 to 1, where 1.0 means complete immunity to knockback.
This mod pins the ceiling at 1.0: on a naked character about 115 flat points, or 100 + 100 across both lines, fill it. Full netherite already contributes 0.4, so you get there faster.

Anything past 1.0 is meaningless, which makes this one of the mod's three functional ceilings (with critical chance 100% and damage reduction 90%): points are still accepted, the effect is capped at 1.0, and the row shows a "!" marker.

pages.title: Flat (numeric) line
text: The curve is LINEAR: +0.00875 per point.
The old curve, gain = 0.35 * x / (x + 40), had an initial slope of 0.35/40 = 0.00875, so the early feel is unchanged.

pages.title: Percent line
text: Also LINEAR: 1.666667 per point, on the DESIGN_BASELINE basis with reference B_ref = 0.20.
The two contributions add up to the attribute value, which is finally clamped to 1.0.

pages.title: Ceiling & returns
text: The ceiling is pinned at 1.0 (complete immunity). It is an intentional functional cap, does not follow the attribute range, and is unaffected by attribute-range mods.
Past 1.0 further points do nothing: the row shows a "!" marker and stat.knockback_resistance.clamped reads true. Points are accepted, the effect is capped - that is the explicit requirement.
This dimension no longer has diminishing returns: both lines are linear, so every point below 1.0 counts in full.

pages.title: Practical advice
text: If you want to stand and trade blows, 0.6..0.8 is already very noticeable: skeleton arrows stop shoving you around and melee mobs struggle to push you off a ledge.
On a naked character the flat line is the better deal (0.1750 for 20 points); in netherite you already hold 0.4 from gear, so check the number before committing.
This line provides no damage reduction at all - it only keeps you standing still.
